name: sluicer
description: The data a web page declares, with where each value came from. No model, no API key.
long_description:
Sluicer reads everything a web page declares about itself -- products, articles, recipes, events, prices, dates, in JSON-LD, microdata, RDFa, OpenGraph and four more vocabularies -- and merges it into one record per thing, every value naming the vocabulary and the place on the page it came from. It learns extractors that fail loudly when a site changes layout, and heals them; audits a page's markup against what Google documents; reads feeds, maps and crawls a site politely. It fetches at the lowest price that works, announces itself by name and obeys robots.txt. No model reads any page, so the same page always gives the same answer. Every tool only reads.

The bundle holds no Python: as the MCPB format's uv runtime says, the host installs Sluicer at this version from PyPI with uv when the extension first starts.

tools.name: extract_declared
tools.description: What a page declares, with provenance, the summary and its conflicts.

tools.name: page_markdown
tools.description: The page's main content as markdown.

tools.name: fetch_page
tools.description: The page's HTML, and whether it took plain HTTP or a browser.

tools.name: compile_extractor
tools.description: An extractor learnt from pages of one template.

tools.name: run_extractor
tools.description: An extractor replayed on a page, checked against what it learnt.

tools.name: heal_extractor
tools.description: The extractor learnt again after a redesign, and what moved.

tools.name: audit_page
tools.description: The page's markup against what Google documents.

tools.name: read_feed
tools.description: A feed's items: RSS, Atom or JSON Feed.

tools.name: map_site
tools.description: A site's addresses, from its sitemaps or its start page's links.

tools.name: crawl_site
tools.description: A site's pages, following its links, each summarised.

allow_private.title: Fetch private addresses
allow_private.description: Let the server fetch localhost, private networks and a cloud's metadata endpoint, which it refuses by default: a page an agent reads can ask it to.

tools.title: Tools to offer
tools.description: Comma-separated tool names, to offer only some of the ten, such as extract_declared,page_markdown. Empty offers all ten.
